name: Timberling Seed
summary: Across Teldrassil, Timberling Seeds are gathered from plant spirits that have grown hostile. Naturalists and druids study them to learn why the forest's plant life has turned aggressive.

sections.title: Seeds of a Restless Forest
sections.body: Timberlings are nature elementals of Teldrassil, and their temper reflects the World Tree's balance. Lately they have grown hostile and angry, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists such as Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth suspect trouble in the soil. They gather seeds from wild timberlings, hoping that purified, carefully tended soil might let docile offspring sprout.

sections.title: A Rooted Corruption
sections.body: Seeds from wild timberlings carry the taint of their corrupted parents. Cenarion scholars such as Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus find that the trouble runs deeper than poor growth. Corruption has taken hold among Teldrassil's plant spirits and throughout the great tree's ecosystem.

faq.answer: A timberling seed is the reproductive kernel of a timberling, a plant-like nature elemental found across Teldrassil. Naturalists gather the seeds to study timberling growth and ecology.
Wild timberlings and bog beasts along the shores and shallows of Lake Al'Ameth yield these seeds.

faq.q: Why does Denalan want timberling seeds?
faq.answer: Denalan suspects poor soil is driving the timberlings to rage. He hopes specially prepared soil will let wild seeds sprout into docile, uncorrupted timberlings.

faq.q: What does Rellian Greenspyre discover about the seeds?
faq.answer: Rellian finds that the seeds carry the taint of their corrupted parents. The corruption is beyond his ability to mend, leaving hope with Denalan's horticultural experiments.

angles.text: As a druid, you can read the tainted seeds as an early warning of unnatural corruption among Teldrassil's plant elementals, a grave concern for the Cenarion Enclave's protectors.
As an herbalist, you can study the seeds to see how soil conditions and ambient corruption affect wild flora.
